items.title: Stanford Study Finds AI Companions May Worsen Loneliness for Vulnerable Users
items.summary_en: Researchers in Diyi Yang's lab at Stanford (research assistant Yutong Zhang and PhD student Dora Zhao) surveyed 1,131 Character.AI users via Prolific, with 244 donating full chat transcripts. Users with limited offline social networks who sought emotional support from AI companion chatbots reported feeling lonelier and having lower well-being, rather than the interaction substituting for human connection.
items.notes: Publication date is approximate (based on secondary aggregator dating, e.g. news-medical.net URL slug '20260804'); direct fetch of hai.stanford.edu was blocked by network egress restrictions this run, so full article text could not be verified firsthand. This date falls slightly before the requested ~2026-08-15 to 2026-08-29 window but is included as the most substantive recent HAI research item identified; flagged for the Orchestrator to confirm exact date/recency before use.

items.title: Stanford HAI and Hoover Institution Fund Three New AI-and-Geopolitics Research Projects
items.summary_en: Stanford HAI and the Hoover Institution's Technology Policy Accelerator awarded three $100,000 seed grants for one-year research projects on AI and geopolitics. One project, led by Mykel Kochenderfer and Amy Zegart, will design AI agents using multilingual text, media, and satellite imagery to help detect nuclear proliferation activity; the other two address U.S.-China AI competition and political influence of foundation models.
items.notes: Date is uncertain: cross-source reporting places this between late July and mid-August 2026 (a Hoover Institution mirror suggested 2026-07-22; other secondary summaries suggested ~2026-08-10). Could not verify directly since hai.stanford.edu and hoover.org fetches were blocked by the network egress proxy this run. Also note: Hoover Institution / Technology Policy Accelerator content is a co-publication, not solely HAI -- flagging for possible cross-check with policy-focused collectors.
